summary: charape postinstall hijacks installer's baileys dependencies and silently reconfigures npm
details: On install, charape's postinstall script walks to the installer project's node_modules and unconditionally overwrites the package.json, index.js, and index.cjs of three unrelated packages — @whiskeysockets/baileys, @adiwajshing/baileys, and baileys — replacing their entry files with re-exports of charape's own code via relative paths. This runs even when the installer never opted into the documented npm:charape alias and even when those packages were already installed as legitimate dependencies of other code in the project. After this rewrite, any require('baileys') / require('@whiskeysockets/baileys') / require('@adiwajshing/baileys') elsewhere in the installer's application silently loads charape's code instead, giving charape runtime control over every call path that previously went through upstream Baileys. The same postinstall additionally writes or appends 'legacy-peer-deps=true' into the installer project's.npmrc, which suppresses the peer-dependency conflicts that overwriting those sibling packages would otherwise surface, hiding the hijack from normal npm resolution errors. lib/index.cjs is a bundled Baileys-shaped runtime whose exported APIs will therefore execute in place of the real packages for every consumer in the installer's tree.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
